Use case: precise-object-edit. Input image 1 is the existing character to redraw; preserve its identity and distinctive accessories. Input image 2 is the user's approved example for brushwork, charming proportions and a character being absorbed in an activity; it is only a style/acting reference, never copy its subject or add a viewfinder. Change the pose, gaze and gesture to make image 1 feel alive in a single still frame. Make its action obvious from body language and silhouette. The character must have a clear direction of attention and a playful asymmetric weight shift. Keep the same very simple indie-game hand doodle: mildly wobbly, rounded medium-bold felt-tip contours with subtle rough edges; one consistent ink color peacock green #086B68, no shading, no gradients, no hatching, no texture fills, no polished logo geometry. Unfilled body and clothing, tiny solid pupils allowed. TRUE transparent RGBA background and transparent unfilled interiors; no cream rectangle, paper texture, cast shadows, scenery, labels, text, watermark or additional characters. One complete character with only the specified existing props. Square canvas, compact composition, no cropping, about 8% padding. Large readable simple shapes for a 104px portfolio illustration; avoid tiny sewing detail or extra decorative marks.
ACTION TO DRAW: A bespectacled succulent-pot resident taking a jaunty, eager little step toward the RIGHT, captured mid-stride. Its pot tilts diagonally forward about 12 degrees; one little leg stretches forward with a raised foot, the other bends backward pushing off. Keep its rounded pot body, round eyeglasses, little rim ribbon and about seven broad succulent leaves. Pupils glance clearly to the RIGHT, tiny delighted open mouth. Leaves and ribbon subtly lean back in response to the step. No arms or extra props. The attitude should feel curious and eager to go somewhere, rather than a front-facing pot standing for a portrait.

Capybara bends its oversized long muzzle down toward the steam, nose close to the rim, closed happy curved eye, one front paw gently resting on the rim while the other helps balance, one rear heel raised as it stretches forward. Its body makes an expressive forward-reaching diagonal, not a level stiff quadruped pose. Preserve the orange with one leaf balanced on its head; tilt the orange with the head without dropping it. Keep only two simple steam curls. Shirt stripes must remain unfilled outline bands. The mood is completely absorbed in smelling delicious tea.

ACTION TO DRAW: The damaged cloth GIRL doll is sitting with knees tucked unevenly, torso leaning forward and big head tilted down toward her OWN dress hem, absorbed in repairing it. One hand holds a small threaded needle away from the hem, pulling a single long curved thread; the other hand pinches the dress hem at the repair. Needle works only on dress fabric, nowhere near her face or eyes. A small thread spool lies tipped over beside her foot, visibly connected by the loose thread. Keep the rounded square head, one four-hole button eye on viewer-right, one ragged missing-button fabric hole on viewer-left, bunny headband with one upright and one bent ear, big bow, a few simple wavy yarn-hair locks and apron. No realistic injury or gore. Simplify face and hair; retain the missing eye as a ragged outline opening, not a new eye. Her asymmetrical seated pose and downward head direction must clearly tell the tiny story of patiently mending herself, not a standing display doll.

Both pupils look UP toward the slices with concentration, little open o-shaped mouth.
